name: Fifty equal spheres in a cube
description: Place the centres of 50 equal, non-overlapping spheres inside a unit cube so that their common radius is as large as possible. The best known packing, with radius 0.1359545126417, is credited to Hugo Pfoertner and is not proven optimal.

sources.locator: Gensane (2004), Dense packings of equal spheres in a cube: the problem, its equivalence with spreading points in a cube, and record packings for N up to 32.

E. Specht, Packomania table of equal spheres in a cube (last update 2026-10-08), row N = 50: radius 0.135954512641663590961947158274, credited to H. Pfoertner (reference [7], 2005); coordinates in scu/txt/scu50.txt.

requirements.datasets: None; the record value is embedded as a parameter and no file is read at evaluation time.

evaluation.benchmark: Fifty equal spheres in a cube
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: construct() -> array of shape (N, 3): centres of N equal spheres inside the cube [-1/2, 1/2]^3 (side 1). Score: the largest common radius r = min(min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, min_i min_k (1/2 - |c_ik|)) for which the spheres are disjoint and inside the cube, computed in double precision; maximize. A centre on or outside the cube, coincident centres, a wrong shape or non-finite values make the candidate invalid.

limitations: Optimality is proven only for a few small N (for example N = 14, Joós 2009); the Packomania table was being revised on 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-08 with new submissions for other sizes, so it may change.

The record coordinates are public (Packomania), so a candidate can reproduce the record from memory or by downloading it beforehand; scores measure the returned construction, not the search that produced it.

Scores are double-precision radii of the returned centres. A score above the record by at most 1e-11 is reported as a tie; a larger gain is a candidate new record that should be confirmed in higher precision and submitted to the record table before it is claimed.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process and is trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes the radius from the returned array but does not sandbox the program.

state_of_the_art.statement: The best known packing of 50 equal spheres in a unit cube has sphere radius 0.135954512641663590961947158274 (Packomania, last update 2026-10-08), credited to Hugo Pfoertner (table reference dated 2005). No optimality proof is known.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find the largest common radius of 50 non-overlapping equal spheres inside a cube (equivalently, spread 50 points in a cube).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Dense packings of equal discs and spheres in containers are classical problems of discrete geometry and models of confined hard-particle systems; optima are proven only for small N, and record tables kept for decades are still being improved by new global-optimisation methods.

papers.title: Dense packings of equal spheres in a cube

papers.task_relation: It defines the problem and the record conventions that the task scores for N = 50 and 100.
